title: Synthetic probe playbook: dashboard calibration for inference workloads
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a working playbook for designing, running, and interpreting synthetic user probes specifically targeted at calibrating tenant-aware inference dashboards and tracing anchors. The intent is not to replace canaries or production SLIs but to provide a predictable, low-cost signal that helps QA/obs teams: (a) validate dashboard widgets after changes, (b) exercise edge-case tracing paths (fanout, fallback, cold-KV cache), and (c) estimate query-cost impact of new batching/quantization policies.

Audience:
- Observability engineers
- SREs who own inference platform dashboards
- Release engineers validating rollout telemetry
- Solutions engineers running tenant-facing experiments

Non-goals:
- Act as the SLO source of truth for customer-facing SLAs.
- Replace full production load tests.

High-level approach:
1) Define a small set of canonical probes that exercise orthogonal code paths (short/long prompt, multi-model fanout, KV-cache warm vs cold, fallback to smaller model). Keep probe payloads stable and checked into repo.
2) Run probes from an isolated probe pool (dedicated agent instances) that are labeled by tenant-sim/feature-flag state.
3) Capture both metrics and trace spans for each probe. Tag payloads with probe_id, probe_type, and expected-path metadata so dashboards can filter and compare.
4) Use probe runs to validate widget thresholds, sampling heuristics, and dashboard query performance before and after instrumentation changes.

Probe catalog (examples):
- quick-echo-short: 40–60 token prompt, single model, no function calls. Exercises stable hot-path generation. Use to detect cold-start and latency regressions.
- long-chained: 1k token prompt, forces KV-cache segmentation, points to large-seq kernels. Useful for memory/latency tail detection.
- multi-model-split: fanout to model-A for embed + model-B for decode; tests fanout tracing and cross-model attribution.
- fallback-path: intentionally route to an unsupported format to trigger fallback routing and small-model substitution.
- cold-cache-warmup: same prompt repeated N times with long idle gap to measure cache warmth dynamics and cost-per-token delta.

Probe metadata fields (stored with each run):
- probe_id: stable id (e.g., probe-20251105-quick-echo-short)
- probe_type: one of [short, long, fanout, fallback, cache-warmup]
- expected_model_chain: comma-separated list (string)
- expected_max_latency_ms: string (number in ms)
- cost_estimate_cents: string (estimated token cost for a run)
- owner: primary owner name

Key metrics emitted (define minimal metric names and units):
- probe.request.count (count) — total probe attempts
- probe.request.success (count) — successful completion (status OK)
- probe.request.latency.p50, p95, p99 (ms) — end-to-end probe latency quantiles
- probe.kvcache.hit_rate (ratio 0..1) — observed prefix/KV hits for runs that exercise cache
- probe.fanout.fork_count (count) — number of model calls in fanout flows
- probe.fallback.rate (ratio) — fraction of runs that used fallback model or path
- probe.trace.span_count (count) — span count emitted per run (sanity check to detect missing instrumentation)
- probe.cost.estimated_cents (gauge) — estimated token cost for the run

Tracing anchors & span expectations:
- Each probe run must emit a top-level span: probe.run (attributes: probe_id, probe_type, expected_model_chain).
- Model invocation spans: model.call.* (attributes: model_name, seq_len, tokenizer_tokens).
- KV cache spans: kvcache.hit / kvcache.miss (attributes: cache_key, shard_id) — allow sampling but ensure at least 1 in 10 probe runs fully records kvcache spans for verification.
- Fallback span: routing.fallback (attributes: reason, fallback_model) — should be recorded when fallback is exercised.
- Fanout: each child model.call span must carry probe_id to link into top-level probe.run trace.

Dashboard calibration guidance:
- Baseline widgets: build a dedicated "Probe Health" dashboard with: probe.request.count (by probe_type), probe.request.success rate, p95/p99 latency heatmap, kvcache.hit_rate trend, and probe.trace.span_count distribution.
- Widget thresholds: use probe historical runs to set alert thresholds (e.g., p95 > baseline*1.5, fallback.rate > 0.02).
- Cost panels: show probe.cost.estimated_cents and rolling 7-day cost to detect runaway synthetic costs after instrumentation changes.
- Lightweight investigation view: single-click drilldown from a latency alert to the last 50 probe traces (sampled) with auto-expanded model.call spans.
- Query budget: ensure dashboard queries for Probe Health use downsampled sources or precomputed rollups to avoid driving query costs in production observability clusters.

Calibration experiments (example plans):
- Experiment A: before/after kernel change
  - Run probe set hourly for 72 hours pre-change and 72 hours post-change.
  - Compare p95/p99, kvcache.hit_rate, and probe.trace.span_count.
  - Expected outcome: p95 improves or stays within 5% of baseline; no drop in kvcache.hit_rate.
- Experiment B: rollout of batching policy
  - Run fanout and short probes at varying concurrency (1, 5, 20 simulated concurrent probes).
  - Capture probe.fanout.fork_count and latency quantiles.
  - Use results to tune batching window and threshold.

Investigation playbook (when probe alerts fire):
1) Check probe.request.count — ensure alert isn’t from missing runs.
2) Inspect probe.request.success rate and error messages in probe logs (linked in probe spans).
3) Open last 20 probe traces; verify top-level probe.run and child model.call spans are present and not truncated.
4) If kvcache.hit_rate dropped, compare cold-cache warmup runs and identify keys with high miss rates.
5) If fallback.rate increased, inspect routing reason and check model variant availability in the target region.
6) Create a lightweight incident note in the observations board and assign to owner in probe metadata.

Operational constraints and guardrails:
- Synthetic probes must not impersonate real tenants or include PII. Use sanitized prompt templates and a dedicated synthetic-tenant id.
- Keep total synthetic probe traffic < 0.5% of platform capacity in a region; use rate-limits.
- Billback: tag probe runs so cost shows in an internal billing view and is excluded from customer-facing usage dashboards.
- Data retention: keep detailed probe traces for 30 days; aggregated metrics rollup for 90 days.

Open questions / discussion points:
- What sample rate for kvcache spans balances cost vs correctness? Proposal: 10% full kv spans, 100% top-level probe.run.
- Should synthetic probes be allowed on Dedicated clusters or run exclusively in hosted infra? Ops input needed for compliance-sensitive customers.
- How to best expose probe health to non-obs teams without noise? Propose a short weekly digest instead of per-alert notifications.
